description: Four bright-field TEM micrographs of annealed 0Cr and 6Cr low-density steel strips after tensile fracture, arranged 2x2 with white panel labels (a)-(d). (a) 0Cr: dense parallel slip bands in the austenite matrix, a yellow double-headed arrow labelled {111} marking the band trace, and a top-right SAED inset labelled [110]; scale bar 500 nm. (b) 0Cr: a dark, heavily deformed band crossing the field with two white arrows; scale bar 500 nm. (c) 6Cr: a grain boundary that slip bands cross; two red circles on opposite sides of the boundary are each joined by a red line to a SAED inset, both labelled [110], and a yellow double-headed arrow labelled {111} spans the boundary; scale bar 200 nm (higher magnification than the other panels). (d) 6Cr: two white arrows marking microbands among dislocation tangles in the austenite matrix; scale bar 500 nm. No numeric data values are printed on any panel - only scale bars and zone-axis labels. The group makes one argument: after tensile fracture the 0Cr and 6Cr structures are similar (slip bands plus prominent microbands), so kappa-carbides play a weak role at final strain.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is a BF TEM micrograph of 0Cr steel with a 500 nm scale bar, showing closely spaced parallel slip bands and a top-right SAED inset labelled [110].
A yellow double-headed arrow labelled {111} marks the slip-band trace in panel (a) and again in panel (c).
Panel (c) is the only panel printed with a 200 nm scale bar; panels (a), (b) and (d) each carry a 500 nm scale bar.
Panel (c) contains two SAED insets, both labelled [110], each connected by a red line to a red circle placed on opposite sides of a grain boundary.
White arrows marking microbands appear in panel (b) (two arrows) and panel (d) (two arrows), while no white arrows appear in (a) or (c).
No numeric values (stress, strain, misorientation) are printed anywhere on the panels; the only printed figures are the scale bars 500 nm, 500 nm, 200 nm and 500 nm.

The caption states the panels show: (a) slip bands in 0Cr steel strips, (b) intersections between ferrite and microbands in 0Cr steel strips, (c) shearable grain boundary in 6Cr steel strips, (d) microbands in 6Cr steel strips.
The citing text states the SADPs along the [110] zone axis on both sides of the grain boundary in Fig. 14(c) indicate a low-angle grain boundary with a misorientation of 2.56 degrees.
The citing text states the true strains of the 0Cr and 6Cr steel strips are 0.255 and 0.298 respectively.
The citing text asserts that besides numerous slip bands, many microbands (marked with white arrows) appear in the austenite matrix of both 0Cr and 6Cr steel strips, as shown in Fig. 14(b) and (d).

The citing text attributes the hardening at the final strain stage to well-developed microbands consisting of large numbers of dislocations, and describes dislocation entanglements at the ferrite/austenite phase boundary due to inconsistent deformation.
The citing text states the 0Cr and 6Cr microstructures are similar after tensile fracture, confirming that the effect of kappa-carbides is very weak at the final strain stage.
In panel (c) the slip bands can be seen continuing across the boundary between the brighter and darker grains, consistent with the caption's 'shearable grain boundary'.

subfigures.description: BF TEM micrograph of annealed 0Cr steel strip after tensile fracture showing densely spaced parallel slip bands in the austenite matrix. A yellow double-headed arrow labelled {111} marks the band trace direction. Top-right inset is an SAED pattern labelled [110]. Scale bar 500 nm.

BF TEM micrograph of 0Cr steel strip showing a broad dark, heavily deformed band (microbands) intersecting lighter deformed regions; two white arrows point to features within the band. Scale bar 500 nm.

BF TEM micrograph of 6Cr steel strip at higher magnification (200 nm scale bar) showing slip bands crossing a grain boundary. Two red circles on either side of the boundary are linked by red lines to two SAED insets, both labelled [110]. A yellow double-headed arrow labelled {111} spans the boundary.
BF TEM micrograph of 6Cr steel strip showing microbands marked by two white arrows within a matrix containing dense dislocation tangles and slip bands. Scale bar 500 nm.

unreadable_items: Panels (b): the ferrite/austenite phase boundary asserted by the caption cannot be distinguished by eye in the printed micrograph - only a dark deformed band is visible
SAED insets in (a) and (c): only the [110] zone-axis label is legible; individual diffraction spots are not indexed, so the 2.56 degree misorientation cannot be verified from the pixels
No magnification values are printed; only scale bars are available
